intro: A generative language model written from first principles: character-level tokenization and an auto-regressive data pipeline, then scaled dot-product attention, a Transformer block, and the same model re-run on a BPE vocabulary.
noteLead: Tensor shapes · attention math · failure modes - all on

stages.title: Vocabulary & Tokenization
stages.summary: Character-level encoder over the raw corpus: unique token set, bijective maps, encode / decode with round-trip verification.
items: stoi (char -> int) and itos (int -> char) built from the sorted unique token set
encode(text) -> list[int] and decode(tokens) -> str
Round-trip check: decode(encode(s)) == s
Small vocabulary (~65 symbols), zero out-of-vocabulary tokens, long sequences as the trade-off
Byte Pair Encoding added later in the same file: byte-level base vocabulary plus learned merges

stages.title: Data Pipeline & Batching
stages.summary: Corpus to a torch.long tensor with a 90 / 10 split and a batch sampler over fixed context windows.
items: Encoded corpus read once into a 1D torch.long tensor
Train / validation split (90% / 10%) to catch overfitting early
get_batch(split, batch_size, block_size) -> x, y with shape (B, T)
Autoregressive pairs: x = data[i : i+T], y = data[i+1 : i+T+1] - T predictions per window
Tokenizer injected, so the same pipeline serves both the character and the BPE run

stages.title: Baseline Bigram Model
stages.summary: An attention-free lookup table that exercises the whole pipeline end to end and sets the loss baseline to beat.
items: Embedding + linear head: logits (B, T, V) against targets (B, T)
Flatten for cross-entropy: (B * T, V) vs (B * T)
Training loop: forward -> loss -> zero_grad -> backward -> step
Autoregressive generation loop sampling from the last position
4000 steps on CPU: loss 4.32 -> 1.51

stages.title: Self-Attention from Scratch
stages.summary: Scaled dot-product attention with a causal mask, first as one head, then as parallel heads concatenated through an output projection.
items: Q / K / V linear projections without bias, head_size channels per head
Scaling by 1 / sqrt(head_size) keeps the softmax out of saturation
Causal mask as a registered buffer, masked_fill with -inf before the softmax
Single head first (head_size = 64), then 4 parallel heads (head_size = 16)
Heads concatenated and projected back to n_embed with a single Linear

stages.title: The Transformer Block
stages.summary: Pre-LayerNorm blocks with residual connections, learned position embeddings, stacked L layers and a linear projection back to the vocabulary.
items: Token embedding + learned position embedding, summed before the first block
Pre-LN residual block: x = x + Attention(LayerNorm(x))
Second residual: x = x + FeedForward(LayerNorm(x))
FeedForward as Linear(64, 256) -> ReLU -> Linear(256, 64)
4 blocks stacked in an nn.Sequential with a final LayerNorm, trained on CUDA

stages.title: Optimization & Training System
stages.summary: AdamW with a cosine learning-rate schedule and warmup, a no-grad validation loop, and checkpoint save / reload for long runs.
items: Trainer class owning the model, the loader and the optimizer
AdamW with zero_grad(set_to_none=True) between steps
Loss printed every 500 iterations - the loss traces on the project page are those prints
Device selected from torch.cuda.is_available(), CUDA run through setup_cuda.bat
experiments.py sweeps tokenizer x architecture and writes the results to JSON

stages.title: Inference & Text Sampling
stages.summary: Greedy decoding, temperature scaling and top-k filtering, with a KV-cache so generation stays linear instead of quadratic.
items: Autoregressive loop sampling from softmax with torch.multinomial
Context trimmed to the last block_size tokens, so generation can run past the window
Text decoded back through whichever tokenizer produced the ids
Still to do: temperature, top-k / top-p filtering and a KV-cache

runsSection.label: Training runs
runsSection.title: Six runs, one model, one corpus
runsSection.intro: Every stage was trained on the same Shakespeare corpus with the same window and the same optimizer, and each run is the terminal output exactly as it came out of the script. Pick a stage to see its loss trace, its log and the text it produced - the log lines are the only checkpointing there was, so the screenshots are the record.
runsSection.caveat: Loss is not comparable across the two tokenizers: the character run scores 65 classes, the BPE run 384, so the BPE curve sits higher on the same axis while buying far more context per window - about 20-25 words instead of 5-7.

runs.title: Bigram, no attention
runs.note: The floor of the whole project: predict a character from the previous character and nothing else. No context, no positions, yet the loss falls to 1.51 - letter statistics alone get most of the way, and the English-looking fragments are pure memorization of spelling patterns.

runs.title: Single-head self-attention
runs.note: One head, three bias-free projections for Q, K and V, scores scaled by 1/sqrt(head_size) and masked with -inf above the diagonal. The attention is not stacking or memory yet, but short real words start surviving - and the rhythm of the verse comes through.

runs.title: Multi-head attention
runs.note: The same head, run four times in parallel with head_size = n_embed / 4 = 16, then concatenated and projected back to n_embed. Different heads settle on different patterns - punctuation, agreement, character names - and the scene structure (speaker lines, blank-line breaks) becomes much more stable.

runs.title: Multi-head + feed-forward
runs.note: Attention only mixes information between tokens - it contains no nonlinearity of its own. The feed-forward net adds one per token: Linear(64, 256) -> ReLU -> Linear(256, 64), a 4x expansion that gives the network room to represent more. Loss ends higher here simply because this run had more parameters to fit in the same 4000 steps.

runs.title: Four stacked Transformer blocks
runs.note: The full block: x = x + Attention(LayerNorm(x)) then x = x + FeedForward(LayerNorm(x)), four of them in a row plus a final LayerNorm before the head. Pre-LN plus residual connections is what makes depth trainable at all - and it runs on the GPU. Four thousand steps is not much for a four-layer model, which is exactly why the curve is still descending when it ends.

runs.title: Byte Pair Encoding tokenizer
runs.model: 4 x Pre-LN block, same as run 05
runs.note: Same network, same window, different tokenizer: bytes as the base vocabulary plus 128 learned merges, so whole words and common suffixes become single tokens. The window now holds roughly 20-25 words instead of 5-7 - and the output finally spells things correctly while keeping the dramatic vocabulary intact.
